skeleton:
Chakchouka Wrap

Tunisian · Easy · Serves 3

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
Chakchouka — eggs poached in a spiced pepper-tomato pan — is the Maghreb's morning canon, and this record is its street format: the same pan's contents, cooked down drier, spooned into bread with the eggs broken over, wrapped, and eaten walking. The sit-down dish (#61, this site's own record) carries the full method; the wrap's work is the reduction and the fold.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

- **Cook the pan down drier than the plated chakchouka.** The #61 dish wants a saucy pan for bread-dipping; the wrap wants its filling to hold — cook the pepper-tomato base 5 extra minutes, until a spoon's trail holds and no pool remains. Wet filling soaks a walking wrap. - **The bridge:** the eggs bridge nothing; the peppers can run all red, all green, or mixed — the Tunisian originals run green peppers and the stronger caraway, and both roads are honest.

Chakchouka Wrap

Prep: 10 minutes · Cook: 25 minutes · Total: About 35 minutes · Serves 3

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 3 tbsp olive oil (about 40 g); 1 onion (about 150 g), sliced; 2 cloves garlic (about 8 g), sliced
  • 2 red or green peppers (about 250 g), sliced in ribbons; 4 ripe tomatoes (about 400 g), grated
  • 1 tsp cumin; 1 tsp sweet paprika; ½ tsp caraway (the Tunisian note); ½ tsp harissa (#91) or chile flakes
  • 1 tsp salt; 4 eggs (about 200 g)
  • 3 rounds of bread (about 200 g) — batbout (#21), khobz, or a wrap's honest flatbread; coriander (about 10 g), lemon

Instructions

  1. **Build the base (20 minutes).** Soften the onion and peppers in the oil over medium — 10 patient minutes to silk — then the garlic, spices, and tomatoes, and cook 10 more until the pan is thick and the oil's red-gold at the edges. Season. Checkpoint — the base should mound briefly on the spoon — the wrap's filling, not a soup — and taste forward: sweet pepper, cumin, caraway's anise whisper, the harissa's hum.
  2. **Eggs, two ways (5 minutes).** Make two wells in the pan, crack the eggs in, lid 3 minutes to just-set whites and molten yolks — for the wrap, the eggs should run less than the plated version, so 4 minutes' lid, the yolks barely thickened. Checkpoint — whites set, yolks creamy-thick: a fully molten yolk floods a wrap; a just-thickened one sauces it from within.
  3. **Wrap and eat (immediately).** Each bread round: a spoon of the base, an egg broken over it with the edge of the spoon, coriander and a lemon squeeze, then folded — twice, into a tight packet — and eaten hot from the hand. Checkpoint — eating test: the bread's soft wall, the pepper-tomato's sweet-spice depth, the egg's richness breaking through in streaks, the coriander's green and lemon's cut at the swallow. It should be the #61 pan's whole argument made portable, and the filling's dryness — the small discipline — is what makes the format honest.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Wrap sogged throughBase too wet, yolk too moltenThe 5-extra-minute reduction; the 4-minute yolk
Filling spilled at the foldOver-stuffedOne egg and a spoon of base per wrap
Wrap tastes flatCaraway or coriander shyBoth carry the Tunisian register

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The base keeps 3 days (the make-ahead — eggs poached to order, wrapped to the minute). Built wraps wait no one. - Variations: the merguez-added version (the #4's sausage), the cheese-melted modern one. The #61 chakchouka and the #86 ojja are this wrap's parents on this site.
